arm_0c_equal_weight_never_traded.definition: Equal-weight, fully-invested, never-traded floor. Starting capital ($100,000) divided into 16 equal shares ($6,250 each), one per ALL16 ticker. Each slice buys shares of its ticker at the closing price on that ticker's FIRST call_date within the locked 195-event population (not the ticker's IPO/listing date, not the simulator's window start of 2022-01-01 -- if a ticker's first in-population call is mid-window, its slice sits as uninvested cash until that date, mirroring how Arm 0b/0 cannot act before a ticker's first call either). No commissions, no taxes, no rebalancing, no reinvestment of dividends (none of the ALL16 pay a dividend material to this window). Final value = sum over 16 tickers of shares_i * price_on(ticker_i, 2024-06-12). Bypasses the allocator, the trend layer and the analyst entirely -- does not run through run_session_sweep_cell.
arm_0c_equal_weight_never_traded.seed: deterministic, no randomness -- no seed needed

cash_deployment_diagnostics_c1.definition: For arm_0b, arm_0 and the control (all three already produced by run_session_sweep_cell / value_attribution_v2_driver.py's run path), read DailySnapshot.cash_total / DailySnapshot.total_value at every daily snapshot in results['daily_snapshots'] to get a cash-share time series and a deployment curve. 'Never invested' for Arm 0b is approximated as (final DailySnapshot.cash_total) / initial_capital, labeled explicitly as an approximation -- Arm 0b's forced-Hold mechanism means no cash placed by session K is ever later deployed, so cash outstanding at window-close is a lower bound on capital that sat idle for the whole remainder of the window, not a precise 'never touched' count.
cash_deployment_diagnostics_c1.return_per_dollar_year_invested: For each arm: (final_value - initial_capital) / integral of daily invested-dollars over the window in dollar-years (sum over days of (total_value - cash_total)/365.25). Reported alongside each arm's final_value, not as a replacement for it.

cash_parked_arm.definition: The real (control) system, identical in every decision it makes (final_action, position sizing, funding order, trend layer, allocator -- none of it re-run or modified). Built as a POST-HOC OVERLAY on the control run's own daily_snapshots.cash_total series, not by re-invoking the allocator with a different funding source: at each session snapshot date, if cash_total rose since the previous snapshot, the increase is parked in SPY at that date's cached close; if cash_total fell (the allocator's own decisions consumed cash), SPY is sold back first, up to the dollar amount needed, at that date's close, before anything else. This never changes what the allocator decided and never redeploys idle cash into existing positions -- the closed 'Never Do' in DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md concerns proportional redeployment of trim/idle cash into existing portfolio POSITIONS; parking in the benchmark index is a measurement device, explicitly not that.
cash_parked_arm.granularity: Session-level (~30 days between snapshots, K=30) -- the same granularity DailySnapshot already carries (recorded once per session, not daily). This driver does not attempt intra-session SPY timing.
cash_parked_arm.benchmark_ticker: SPY, from the existing frozen price_cache.json (no cache refresh).
cash_parked_arm.seed: deterministic, no randomness -- no seed needed
cash_parked_arm.shortfall_handling: If SPY market value at a snapshot is insufficient to cover a funding need (shortfall > 0), the driver records it explicitly rather than allowing the arm to silently exceed available capital. A nonzero shortfall_total in the manifest is a finding, not expected under normal operation given the control's own cash never goes structurally negative.

arm_0c_cash_share_fill.definition: Arm 0c (equal-weight, 16 slices, never traded) DOES carry idle cash: each ticker's $6,250 slice sits at face value (uninvested) from the window start (2022-01-01) until that ticker's own first call_date in the 195-event population, then converts to shares and is marked to market for the remainder of the window. stage_d.injection_point: per_call_rec, NOT final_action. Concretely: sweep_cadence_and_session_model.recompute_trend_layer(events, tier_fn, extra_fields) is called AFTER overwriting each overridden event's .per_call_rec / .thesis_health / .recommended_size and after building a matching extra_fields entry (fresh_money_allocation / credibility_delta / mitigation_track_record / stumble_type) -- so compute_trend_verdict()/apply_matrix() (the real, unmodified trend layer) compute final_action from the oracle's per_call_rec exactly as they would from a real analyst's per_call_rec. This is confirmed against sweep_cadence_and_session_model.py lines 85-111 (recompute_trend_layer) and line 782 (run_session_sweep_cell reads event.final_action, which recompute_trend_layer already set).

label_encoding.bound_direction: BOUND-LOOSENING. Mapping bearish to 'Exit' gives the oracle full de-risking on every correctly-called decline -- a stronger action than any real call in this corpus ever issued for a bearish outcome (13.9% catch rate at Trim/Exit combined, per Stage B). A 'Trim'-only encoding would produce a strictly lower ceiling. This inflates the reported ceiling versus the floor of what 'perfect direction calls, using only the real vocabulary's weakest sell action' could mean.

non_direction_field_synthesis.definition: For every event this arm overrides, thesis_health / credibility_delta / stumble_type / mitigation_track_record / fresh_money_allocation / recommended_size are all set to the single most SUPPORTIVE value consistent with the label (see ORACLE_SYNTHESIS dict in the driver: bullish -> Strengthening/positive/None/strong/100/35; neutral -> Intact/neutral/None/mixed/50/15; bearish -> Broken/negative/Structural/unproven/0/0), never reused from the real (possibly conflicting) fields the actual call carried.
non_direction_field_synthesis.why_it_moves_results: compute_trend_verdict() and compute_final_confidence() read these fields (via the per-ticker `history` list built in recompute_trend_layer) to decide trend overrides and confidence; final_confidence and thesis trajectory feed rank_key(), which orders swap-funding donor selection and therefore which positions get displaced to fund a candidate. A conflicting real field (e.g. a bearish call paired with a real fresh_money_allocation that looks confident) could trigger a downward override or de-prioritize funding even on a directionally-correct oracle call.
non_direction_field_synthesis.bound_direction: BOUND-LOOSENING. Making every field maximally consistent with the label removes the friction/override risk a genuinely noisy analyst call would sometimes trigger against itself, which can only raise or leave unchanged the resulting final_action's alignment with the oracle's direction -- never lower it.

arms_this_stage.D-both: Every event in the 195-event population gets its oracle label's full synthesis (bullish/bearish/neutral per event, independent of the real call).
arms_this_stage.D-up: Only events whose oracle label is 'bullish' get the synthesis; every other event keeps the REAL per_call_rec / thesis_health / recommended_size / extra_fields exactly as load_events_dedup_on() produced them.
arms_this_stage.D-down: Only events whose oracle label is 'bearish' get the synthesis; every other event keeps the real call.
